instruction.text: Class 5A is comparing the dissolution rates of salt in 2 beakers containing the same amount of water. They stir the salt in the beaker on the left with a spoon and let the salt in the beaker on the right dissolve naturally. Answer the questions.

hint.text: The dissolution rate is how quickly a soluble solid dissolves in a liquid.
hint.label: Dissolution rate

atoms.a: In which beaker has the salt dissolved faster?
The pupils had hypothesised that stirring would make the salt dissolve more slowly. Were they correct?

feedback.end: Stirring a soluble solid into a solution makes it dissolve significantly faster.

atoms.b: The ((++volume colour)) of liquid also influences the ((++quantity quality)) of a soluble solid that can dissolve.
Increasing the volume of the liquid will allow for a ((++larger smaller)) quantity to dissolve.

instruction.text: Class 5B is comparing the dissolution rates of salt in 3 glasses of water. Sort the glasses by the quantity of salt that will dissolve in them. Start with the largest quantity at the top.

hint.text: The dissolution rate is how quickly a soluble solid dissolves in a liquid.
hint.label: Dissolution rate

atoms.a: The pupils had hypothesised that more salt would dissolve in a greater volume of water. Were they correct?

instruction.text: Decide if the following statements are true or false.

atoms.a: Decreasing the volume of a liquid allows a larger quantity of a soluble solid to dissolve.
Stirring a soluble solid into a liquid makes it dissolve more slowly
